lines.japanese: 夕刻、僕らは柳木原に帰ってきた。
lines.english: By evening, we had returned to Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 「今度は渡来さんを僕の家族に紹介するよ」
lines.english: “Next time, I'll introduce you to my family.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　嫌そう？」
lines.english: “Hm? You don't want me to?”

lines.japanese: 「や、や、それはない。ないんだけど、リアルに考えるとやっぱり……緊張する……」
lines.english: “No, no, that's not it. Not at all. It's just... when I actually imagine it... I get nervous...”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君ち、妹ちゃんいたよね。前に家デンかけたとき、出てもらったことある」
lines.english: “You have a little sister, right? She answered once when I called your home phone.”
“Ah.”
“Ah.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 突然の遭遇。兄妹そろってぽっかり口を開けてしまった。
lines.english: A sudden encounter. Brother and sister stared at each other with our mouths hanging open.

lines.japanese: 小鳩は兄への挨拶も忘れて、その隣りの存在に目を丸くしている。
lines.english: Kobato forgot even to greet her brother. Her eyes went wide at the person beside me.

lines.japanese: 羽田の家のひとたちには、僕にも親しい女の子が出来たことをそれとなく伝えてある。病気のことも隠さず打ちあけた大事なパートナーだと。
lines.english: I had indirectly told the members of the Haneda family that I had become close to a girl. She was an important partner to whom I had revealed my condition without hiding anything.

lines.japanese: その人物をいざ目の当たりにしたら、いろいろ思うところがあったのだろう。容姿とか。
lines.english: Now that they had the person herself before them, they must have had all sorts of thoughts. About her appearance, for example.

lines.japanese: 「学校の帰り？」
lines.english: “On your way home from school?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん……吉川さんと寄り道してた」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah... I stopped somewhere with Yoshikawa.”

lines.japanese: 今日は土曜日。僕らは休みだけど、小鳩の学校は午前中だけ授業があった。
lines.english: Today was Saturday. We had the day off, but Kobato's school held classes in the morning.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、友達？」
lines.english: “A friend of yours, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、丁度よかった。僕の妹を紹介するよ」
lines.english: “Yes. This is perfect timing. Let me introduce my sister.”

lines.japanese: 僕らはオフィス街の静かなコーヒースタンドに場所を変えた。
lines.english: We moved to a quiet coffee stand in the office district.

lines.japanese: カウンターでコーヒーと軽めの茶菓子を頼んで、三人向かいあう。
lines.english: We ordered coffee and light pastries at the counter, then sat facing one another.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ改めて」
lines.english: “All right. Let's start over.”

lines.japanese: 「こちら渡来明日香さん」
lines.english: “This is Asuka Watarai.”
“H-hello...”

lines.japanese: 「で、妹の小鳩」
lines.english: “And this is my sister, Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どもです……」
lines.english: “H-hello...”

lines.japanese: 「あの、こほん、初めまして。渡来です。鷹志さんには、たいへん、お世話になっております」
lines.english: “Ahem. It's a pleasure to meet you. I'm Watarai. Takashi has been very kind to me.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは珍しく硬くなっていた。
lines.english: Watarai was uncharacteristically stiff.

lines.japanese: 「いいい、いえあの、ここ、こちらこそ、つまらない兄ですが、どうぞごえんりょなく」
lines.english: “N-n-no, um, likewise. My brother isn't much, but please don't hold yourself back.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩も例によって硬くなっていた。
lines.english: Kobato was stiff in her usual way.

lines.japanese: そして、どちらからも二の句は出てこなかった。
lines.english: And neither found a second thing to say.

lines.japanese: ふたりとも落ちつきなく上下左右を眺めまわしながら、何度も何度もグラスを口に運んでいた。
lines.english: Both looked restlessly up, down, left, and right, lifting their glasses to their lips over and over.
“Ahaha...?”
“Ehehe...”

lines.japanese: 笑顔でぺこぺこ頭を下げあってるけど、言葉らしい言葉は出てこない。
lines.english: They kept smiling and bobbing their heads at each other, but nothing resembling words came out.

lines.japanese: 「あー、あのー……今日はいい天気だねー？」
lines.english: “Um... Nice weather today, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい、今日はとてもいい天気です！」
lines.english: “Y-yes! The weather is very nice today!”

lines.japanese: やっと交わされた会話は、外国語講座の例文みたいなぎこちなさだった。
lines.english: Their first exchange had all the stiffness of example sentences from a foreign-language course.

lines.japanese: 「ねー、クロワッサン美味しいねー？」
lines.english: “The croissant is good, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ……うん、すごい、すごいおいしいですクロワッサン。すごい、すごいおいしー！」
lines.english: “Oh... Yes. It's really, really good. The croissant is really, really delicious!”

lines.japanese: しかしクロワッサンはまだ一かじりもされていなかった。
lines.english: But Kobato hadn't taken a single bite of it.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、話題」
lines.english: “Haneda. Topic.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あ、そうか」
lines.english: “What? Oh, right.”

lines.japanese: つい見守ってしまった。よく考えたら、僕が率先して回さなきゃいけない立場だ。
lines.english: I had fallen into simply watching them. Thinking about it, I was the one responsible for keeping the conversation moving.

lines.japanese: 「えーと、じゃあ……趣味とか聞く？」
lines.english: “Um, then... Shall we ask about hobbies?”

lines.japanese: 「お見合いかよ」
lines.english: “What is this, an arranged marriage meeting?”

lines.japanese: 「わ、私の趣味は読書です！」
lines.english: “M-my hobby is reading!”

lines.japanese: 「あら素敵。小鳩ちゃんったら文学少女さんなのね」
lines.english: “How lovely. Why, little Kobato, you’re quite the literary young lady.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、いつもと言葉遣いが違うよ」
lines.english: “You're speaking differently from usual, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「そういう日もあると思うわ」
lines.english: “Some days are like that.”

lines.japanese: 「いくらなんでも、渡来さんが女の子にちゃん付けなんて似合わないよ」
lines.english: “No matter the day, adding ‘little’ to a girl's name doesn't suit you, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そっち？　明日香さん、どんだけ男前な印象なの？」
lines.english: “Wait, that’s what you meant? Just how macho do you think I am?”

lines.japanese: 「小鳩も文学少女って感じじゃないよね。趣味は読書、ていうのは嘘じゃないけど」
lines.english: “Kobato doesn't really seem like a literary maiden either. Reading is her hobby, but...”

lines.japanese: 「寝ても覚めてもまんがばかりです」
lines.english: “All I ever read day and night is manga.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、小鳩ちゃん漫画好きなんだ？」
lines.english: “Oh, you like manga, little Kobato?”

lines.japanese: 「ふふッ」
lines.english: “Hehe.”

lines.japanese: 「学校ではまんがクラブに所ぞくしています」
lines.english: “I belong to the manga club at school.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー、じゃあ読むだけじゃなくて、小鳩ちゃんが自分でも……」
lines.english: “Oh. Then you don’t just read it, little Kobato. Do you draw your own—”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふッ」
lines.english: “Hehehe.”

lines.japanese: 「あの、お兄さん？　君はなんでいちいち温かな微笑みを浮かべるの？」
lines.english: “Excuse me, Big Brother? Why do you keep smiling so warmly?”

lines.japanese: 「だって、やっぱり新鮮で。渡来さんなのに、下の名前をちゃん付けって。ふふふふ──」
lines.english: “Because this is so fresh. You, of all people, adding ‘little’ to her name. Hehehehe—”

lines.japanese: 「──いたっ、あ、やめ、やめてよ渡来さん、足踏まないで」
lines.english: “—ow! Stop, Watarai. Don't step on my foot.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、あっ、すみません、お気づかいいただかなくてけっこうです。私のことは、日ごろのように呼びすてしてください」
lines.english: “Oh, um, please don't trouble yourself on my account. You can leave it off and call me the way you normally would.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいやいや、ちゃんが似合う子なら、べつにちゃんぐらい普通に付けるって」
lines.english: “No, no. If it suits a girl, of course I'll use it.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふふ」
lines.english: “Hehehehe.”

lines.japanese: 「いたっ、あ、ごめ、ごめんね渡来さん……」
lines.english: “Ow! S-sorry, Watarai...”

lines.japanese: 「じゃー、あいだを取って『こばっちゃん』でどう？」
lines.english: “Then let’s split the difference and call you ‘Kobbie.’ How about that?”

lines.japanese: 「ふだん着感覚のかざらなさが、わかい子に受けると思われます」
lines.english: “Its casual, unadorned feeling is expected to appeal to young people.”

lines.japanese: 「こばっちゃん、学校では友達になんて呼ばれてるの？」
lines.english: “Kobbie, what do your friends at school call you?”

lines.japanese: 「羽田なので羽田さんです。友だちはそう多くありません」
lines.english: “My name is Haneda, so they call me Haneda. I do not have very many friends.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、同じー。私も渡来だから渡来さん。友達めっちゃ少ない」
lines.english: “Oh, same. I'm Watarai, so they call me Watarai. I've got hardly any friends.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 驚いてる。渡来さんは見るからにきらびやかで、とてもそうは見えないからだろう。
lines.english: Kobato looked surprised. Watarai was visibly glamorous, so she must not have looked that way at all.

lines.japanese: 事実、彼女の場合、一般的な意味での友人は多い方だ。知人と友人の境界が、ひとより遥か高いところにあるっていうだけで。
lines.english: In fact, by an ordinary definition, Watarai had many friends. The boundary she drew between acquaintance and friend merely stood far higher than most people's.

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに私はじょう時ぼしゅう中です」
lines.english: “For the record, I am accepting applications at all times.”

lines.japanese: 「ほんと？　じゃあ私、立候補ー」
lines.english: “Really? Then I volunteer.”

lines.japanese: 八方美人の渡来さんが、真意とはべつにそういった社交上の冗談を口にすることは珍しくない。
lines.english: Sociable with everyone, Watarai often made that sort of polite joke regardless of what she truly meant.

lines.japanese: だけど、僕はずっと彼女といるようになって、少しは彼女の本心が見えるようになったつもりだ。
lines.english: But after spending so much time with her, I believed I had learned to see a little of her true feelings.

lines.japanese: 僕の妹と友達になりたいと言ってくれたその表情は、たぶん偽りなく信じていいものだった。
lines.english: The expression with which she offered to be my sister's friend was one I believed I could trust without reservation.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん、ちょっとトイレ」
lines.english: “Sorry. I'm going to the restroom.”

lines.japanese: もう、少しぐらい仲人が席を外させてもらっても大丈夫だろう。
lines.english: The matchmaker could probably leave them alone for a moment now.

lines.japanese: 僕は店に入ってきたときから催していたものを処理し、改めてすっきりした気分で歓談することにした。
lines.english: I took care of the need I had felt since we entered the shop, then prepared to rejoin the conversation with a newly refreshed spirit.

lines.japanese: エアータオルの突風音が止むと、意外な静寂が訪れた。オフィスビルの一フロアであるこの店は、ＢＧＭを含めあらゆる環境音が控えめだった。
lines.english: When the gale from the hand dryer stopped, an unexpected silence arrived. The shop occupied one floor of an office building, and every ambient sound, including the background music, was subdued.

lines.japanese: 「そりゃそうだよね。そう簡単には割りきれないと思う」
lines.english: “Of course. I don't think that's something you can simply come to terms with.”

lines.japanese: 僕らの席はレストルームの直近だったから、ふたりの話し声も近い。
lines.english: Our table stood close to the restroom, so their voices were close as well.

lines.japanese: 初対面の女の子ふたりはどんな話をしているのだろう。円滑な顔合わせを維持するため、プラス些細ないたずら心が働いて、僕はドアノブに手をかけたまま、つい耳をそばだてた。
lines.english: What were two girls who had just met talking about? Wanting to keep their introduction going smoothly, with a dash of petty mischief added in, I found myself listening with my hand still on the doorknob.

lines.japanese: 「なんとなく『うーん』ってゆうか『え？　え？』ってゆうのが、ずっとあって……」
lines.english: “There was always this feeling like, ‘Hmm,’ or ‘What? What?’...”

lines.japanese: 「うん、違和感ってやつかな」
lines.english: “Yes. I suppose you'd call that a sense of wrongness.”

lines.japanese: 「それです、いわかんです。顔はお兄ちゃんなのに、性格が全ぜんお兄ちゃんじゃなくて、ずっといわかんがあったんです」
lines.english: “That's it. Wrongness. His face was my brother's, but his personality wasn't my brother's at all, so I always felt that wrongness.”

lines.japanese: ノブを握っていた手が、思わず落ちた。
lines.english: My hand dropped from the knob.

lines.japanese: 僕の──僕たちの話だ。
lines.english: They were talking about me—about us.

lines.japanese: 「だからホントゆうと、タカシお兄ちゃんをタカシお兄ちゃんって思えるようになったのは、さいきんのことなんです」
lines.english: “So, to tell the truth, it was only recently that I started thinking of Takashi as Takashi, my brother.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、いまはもうだいじょぶです。いろいろあって、一回お兄ちゃんって呼んだら、なんかいわかんがシュワーってとけてっちゃいました」
lines.english: “Oh, but it is all right now. A lot happened, and once I called him my brother, the wrongness sort of fizzed away.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ。じゃあ、お兄ちゃんが増えて良かったんじゃない？」
lines.english: “I see. Then isn't it good that you gained another brother?”

lines.japanese: 「そう思います」
lines.english: “I think so.”

lines.japanese: 僕の妹は、長年に渡って、兄の病気のことをほとんど誰にも言えずひとりで抱えこんできた。
lines.english: For many years, my sister had borne my illness almost entirely alone, unable to tell anyone.

lines.japanese: 会ってすぐの渡来さんにこんな話をしてるのは、それだけ背負っていた重荷に耐えかねていたのかもしれない。
lines.english: If she could speak about it this openly to Watarai after they had only just met, perhaps the burden she had carried had simply become too heavy.

lines.japanese: 「分かる、なんて私なんかが言うのもおこがましいけど──」
lines.english: “It may be presumptuous for someone like me to say I understand, but—”

lines.japanese: 「おこまがしい？」
lines.english: “Persumptuous?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ナマ言ってんじゃねーぞってことね」
lines.english: “Oh. It means I shouldn’t get too big for my britches.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほどです。おこまがしい、おこまがしい……」
lines.english: “I see. Persumptuous, persumptuous...”

lines.japanese: 小鳩がまたひとつ微妙に間違った日本語を会得しようとしている。渡来さんは気付いてないみたいだから、帰ったら僕がさりげなく訂正してあげよう。
lines.english: Kobato was about to pick up another word slightly wrong. Watarai didn’t seem to notice, so I would quietly correct her when we got home.

lines.japanese: 「だからそう、おこがましいけど、想像してみると分かる気はするんだよね」
lines.english: “Right. It may be presumptuous, but when I imagine it, I feel as if I can understand a little.”

lines.japanese: 「たとえば、うちのお母さんが、お母さんじゃないひとになっちゃうってことでしょ。それは……恐いよね」
lines.english: “Say my mother turned into someone who wasn't my mother. That's... frightening.”

lines.japanese: 「大好きだったひとがいなくなって──ていうか、目の前にいるのにいなくて、その代わり全然違うひとが当然のようにそこにいるわけでしょ。それは、うーん……」
lines.english: “Someone you loved disappeared—or rather, they were right in front of you and still gone—and a completely different person stood there in their place as if that were only natural. That would be... Hmm...”

lines.japanese: 「……やっぱりおこがましいな。その立場を考えたらゾッとするけど、どうしても実感が薄いし。たぶんコレって、こばっちゃんが実際ずーっと味わってきた辛さとか寂しさの比じゃないんだろうね」
lines.english: “...No. It is presumptuous after all. Imagining myself in your place makes me shudder, but it still doesn't feel real. I'm sure that doesn't compare to the pain and loneliness you've actually lived with all this time.”

lines.japanese: 「わかんないけど、すごく……すごく……あれでした」
lines.english: “I do not know, but it was very... very... that.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は懸命に言葉を選んだけれど、適切な単語を見つけだせなかったみたいだ。
lines.english: Kobato searched desperately for words, but apparently couldn't find the right one.

lines.japanese: すごく辛かった。すごく寂しかった。すごく悲しかった。
lines.english: Very painful. Very lonely. Very sad.

lines.japanese: 幼い語彙でどう表現しても、それは、僕たちの存在そのものをことごとく非難することになる。
lines.english: However she expressed it with her young vocabulary, she would be condemning the very existence of every one of us.

lines.japanese: 彼女はヨージ君の帰りを待っている長過ぎた孤独のときでさえ、すり替わってしまった僕らを責めたりしない子だった。
lines.english: Even through the long, lonely years when she waited for Youji to return, she never blamed those of us who had taken his place.

lines.japanese: 「すごく大変だったね」
lines.english: “It must have been so hard.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがシンプルでいてとても優しい言葉を差しだした。
lines.english: Watarai offered words that were simple and very kind.

lines.japanese: けれど小鳩は──
lines.english: But Kobato—

lines.japanese: 「だったと思います。どのお兄ちゃんも、みんな大変だったと思います」
lines.english: “I think so. I think every one of my brothers had it hard.”

lines.japanese: ──その慰労の言葉が、自らに贈られたものだとはすぐに気付けなかった。
lines.english: —did not immediately realize that the words of comfort were meant for her.

lines.japanese: 僕らの妹は、いたわられることに慣れないまま育ってしまったんだ。
lines.english: Our sister had grown up without ever getting used to being cared for.

lines.japanese: 「ううん。違うよ、こばっちゃんが」
lines.english: “No. I mean you, Kobbie.”
“Me?”

lines.japanese: 「もちろん当人たちもそうだろうけど、周りだって同じかそれ以上に大変だったでしょ？」
lines.english: “Of course it was hard on them. But it was just as hard, maybe harder, on the people around them, wasn't it?”

lines.japanese: 大変というのはとても柔軟な日本語だ。すべてを曖昧に包みこんで、尖った角を隠してしてしまう。
lines.english: *Hard* was an extraordinarily flexible word. It wrapped everything in ambiguity and hid every sharp corner.

lines.japanese: あとに残るのは、一塊の漠然としたねぎらいだ。
lines.english: What remained was a single, shapeless mass of sympathy.

lines.japanese: 「大変だったのに、よくがんばったね。こばっちゃん、えらい」
lines.english: “You went through all that, and you did so well. You were wonderful, Kobbie.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ？」
lines.english: “Uh... Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「え、えっ！？　なに？　どうしたの？」
lines.english: “W-wait. What is it? What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: とつぜん渡来さんの声がうろたえだした。
lines.english: Watarai's voice suddenly grew flustered.

lines.japanese: 何事だろう。僕はそっとドアを押す。
lines.english: What had happened? I gently pushed the door open.

lines.japanese: 丸く見開かれた小鳩の瞳が潤んで、その端から小さな雫がひとすじ零れおちていた。
lines.english: Kobato's round, wide eyes had filled with tears. A small drop spilled from one corner and rolled down her cheek.

lines.japanese: 「あ……ごめん、私なんか悪いこと言っちゃった？」
lines.english: “Oh... I'm sorry. Did I say something wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ！　いえ、ちがいます、ぜんぜん！」
lines.english: “No! No, that isn't it at all!”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、なんで……？」
lines.english: “Then why...?”

lines.japanese: 「自分でもわかんない……え？　なんでだろ？　なんか、いまえらいって言われたら、いきなりじわーって来ちゃって」
lines.english: “I don't know... Huh? Why? When you said I was wonderful, it suddenly welled up inside me.”

lines.japanese: 「なんか、びっくりして……だって、がんばったなんて、私そんなふうに言われたこと、一度もなかったから……」
lines.english: “It surprised me... because no one had ever told me I had done well before...”

lines.japanese: 「いままで誰も言ってくれなかったから」
lines.english: “No one ever said it to me.”

lines.japanese: ぎりぎり笑顔を保っていた小鳩の表情が、堰を切ったように崩れた。
lines.english: The smile Kobato had barely held together broke like a burst dam.

lines.japanese: そして涙が溢れだした。
lines.english: And the tears came pouring out.

lines.japanese: 「うん、私大変だった。ほんとはすっごい、いっぱい大変だったよ。ないしょだからだれにも言えなかったけど、ほんとはひとりでいっぱいがんばったんだよ？」
lines.english: “Yes, it was hard for me. It was really, really hard. It was a secret, so I couldn't tell anyone, but I worked so hard all by myself.”

lines.japanese: 「団地のころは、お兄ちゃんのこと知られてたから、色んなひとにいじめられたりこわがられたりして──」
lines.english: “When we lived in the housing complex, people knew about my brother. Lots of them bullied me or were scared of me—”

lines.japanese: 「引っこしてきてからも、お兄ちゃんたち色んなひとに迷わくかけて、私いっぱいあやまったけど、でもないしょだから、ほんとのこと言えなくて、私のせいにされておこられて──」
lines.english: “Even after we moved, my brothers caused trouble for lots of people. I apologized so many times, but it was a secret and I couldn't tell them the truth, so they blamed me and got angry at me—”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん見てないと心配だから、学校から帰っても家から出なかったし、友だちにさそわれても遊びに行かなかったし──」
lines.english: “I was worried if I didn't watch my brother, so even after I got home from school, I never left the house. When friends invited me out, I didn't go—”

lines.japanese: 小鳩が固く鍵をかけてきたものは、呆気ないぐらいに次々と溢れだした。
lines.english: The things Kobato had kept so tightly locked away poured out one after another with startling ease.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがうんうん頷いて安心させている。
lines.english: Watarai kept nodding to reassure her.

lines.japanese: 僕は知っている。明かせない秘密を抱えることは、それだけで凄まじい重責となる。
lines.english: I knew. Merely carrying a secret one could never reveal was an immense responsibility.

lines.japanese: ましてやそれが自身ではない誰かのためだとすれば。
lines.english: All the more when the secret was kept for someone else's sake.

lines.japanese: そしてその守るべき対象にさえ理解されないとすれば。
lines.english: And when even the person one protected did not understand.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん……さいしょのお兄ちゃんいなくなっちゃって、私すごくさびしいのに、あとからどんどんちがうひとばっかり出てきて──」
lines.english: “My brother... My first brother disappeared, and I was so lonely, but then more and more different people kept coming out—”

lines.japanese: 幼かった臆病な少女が、突然現れる見知らぬ男たちにどれほど不安を掻きたてられただろう。
lines.english: How much fear must those unknown men, appearing without warning, have stirred in that young and timid girl?

lines.japanese: ＤＩＤは一般に障害と呼ばれているとおり、決して誰かの意思で冒険活劇になぞらえてコントロールできるような、都合の良いものじゃない。
lines.english: As its general classification as a disorder suggested, DID was never a convenient thing that anyone could consciously control and shape into an adventure story.

lines.japanese: 妹を守るためにヨージ君が意図的に作りだした四人の勇者以外にも、数えきれないほどの人格たちが、偶発的に生まれては奈落の底へ消えている。
lines.english: Beyond the four heroes Youji had deliberately created to protect his sister, countless personalities had arisen by accident and vanished again into the abyss.

lines.japanese: 「へんなひととか、おっかないひともいて──」
lines.english: “Some were weird, and some were scary—”

lines.japanese: 「どなられたり、ぶたれたり、髪ひっぱられたり、あと、あと……あと、いっぱいこわくて……牧師さんの呪文がなかったら、私、死んじゃってたかもしんない」
lines.english: “They yelled at me and hit me and pulled my hair, and... and... so many things were scary... If I hadn't had the pastor's spell, I might have died.”

lines.japanese: 泡のように突如浮かびあがる荒削りの人格には、まっとうな社会性を持たないものもいるという。
lines.english: Some of the rough personalities that surfaced suddenly like bubbles apparently possessed no proper capacity for social behavior.

lines.japanese: 不幸中の幸いというべきか、過去に小鳩が大きな怪我を負ったという話はない。
lines.english: Perhaps it was one mercy amid the misfortune that I had never heard of Kobato suffering a serious physical injury in the past.

lines.japanese: しかし心の傷は深かったのだろう。思えば彼女は、僕らに対するときいつも怯えるような目をしていた。
lines.english: But the wounds to her heart must have run deep. Looking back, she had always watched us with frightened eyes.

lines.japanese: 「でも、お母さんに言ったら、お兄ちゃん病院とかに連れてかれちゃうから、だれにも言えなくて──」
lines.english: “But if I told Mom, they might take my brother away to a hospital, so I couldn't tell anyone—”

lines.japanese: 「私、おっかないひとが表に行こうとするのも、がんばって止めたよ。知らないひとが出てきても、がんばって話したり、ごはん作ったり──」
lines.english: “I worked hard to stop the scary ones when they tried to go outside. Even when a stranger appeared, I tried hard to talk to him or make him food—”

lines.japanese: 「私、ほんとはいっぱいたいへんだったのに、夜ねらんない日もいっぱいあったのに、がんばってることだれにも言えなくて──」
lines.english: “It was really so hard for me, and there were so many nights I couldn't sleep, but I couldn't tell anyone how hard I was trying—”

lines.japanese: 「だれにもがんばったって言ってもらえなくて──」
lines.english: “And no one ever told me I had done well—”

lines.japanese: 「うん、頑張った。大変だったよね。でも、こばっちゃん頑張った。ずーっと頑張ってきた。えらい」
lines.english: “You did. It was hard, wasn't it? But you did so well, Kobbie. You've been doing your best all this time. You were wonderful.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは小鳩の頭を撫でていた。僕はひとり自らの涙を拭っていた。
lines.english: Watarai stroked Kobato's head. Alone, I wiped away my own tears.

lines.japanese: 「今日までずっと、お兄ちゃんを守ってきてくれたね。ありがとう。これからは私にも少し手伝わせてね」
lines.english: “You've protected your brother every day until now. Thank you. From now on, let me help you a little.”

lines.japanese: 「うう、ぐすっ……」
lines.english: “Nn... Sniff...”

lines.japanese: 「う、ううぅ、ひっく……ううっ、ううぅ……」
lines.english: “Nn... Nnn... Hic... Nnn... Nnnn...”

lines.japanese: 僕はそっとドアを閉めて個室へ戻った。
lines.english: I quietly closed the door and returned to the stall.

lines.japanese: このまま飛びだして小鳩のか細い体を抱きしめたい衝動に駆られもしたけど、彼女は相手が渡来さんだから打ちあけたんだ。
lines.english: I felt the urge to rush out and wrap Kobato's slender body in my arms, but she had revealed those things because the person with her was Watarai.

lines.japanese: いままで僕らに黙っていたのは、僕らに知らせたくなかったからだ。だったら彼女がその気にならない限りは、僕も聞かなかったことにしておこう。
lines.english: She had kept silent until now because she didn't want us to know. Then until she chose otherwise, I would pretend I had heard nothing.

lines.japanese: そして治療がすべて終わり、もう妹に世話をかけさせないと誓える日に初めて、これまでのお礼と「がんばったね」を贈らせてもらおう。
lines.english: And when all my treatment was complete, on the day I could swear I would never burden my sister again, I would finally thank her for everything and tell her she had done well.

lines.japanese: だから、いまはまだ、ここで。
lines.english: So for now, I would remain here.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、僕たちのプリンセス」
lines.english: “Thank you, our princess.”

lines.japanese: そのあと僕は、赤くなった目が戻るのを待って洗面所を出た。
lines.english: Afterward, I waited until the redness had left my eyes before emerging from the restroom.

lines.japanese: 席では小鳩がぐすぐす鼻を鳴らしていたが、渡来さんがめちゃめちゃ泣ける少女漫画の話をして泣かせたことになっていた。
lines.english: Kobato was still sniffling at the table, but the official story was that Watarai had made her cry by describing an incredibly moving girls' manga.

lines.japanese: そして三人で、少女漫画や少年漫画や魔女っ子アニメやロボットアニメの話をして盛りあがった。
lines.english: Then the three of us had a lively conversation about girls' manga, boys' manga, magical-girl anime, and robot anime.

lines.japanese: けれど小鳩に笑ってもらいたい気持ちが先走って、つい『軟式文芸部！』の解説に力を入れすぎてしまったのは失敗だったかもしれない。
lines.english: But in my eagerness to make Kobato laugh, I may have gone too far in my impassioned explanation of *Soft-Style Literature Club!*

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが軽く引いていた。
lines.english: Watarai looked mildly disturbed.

lines.japanese: 「あれ、小鳩？　電車乗らないの？」
lines.english: “Hm? Kobato, aren't you getting on the train?”

lines.japanese: 三人で駅まで来て、さあ改札へ、という段になって小鳩の足が止まった。
lines.english: The three of us reached the station, but just as we were about to pass through the gates, Kobato stopped.

lines.japanese: 「うん。私、夕ごはんの買いものして帰る」
lines.english: “No. I am going to buy groceries for dinner and then go home.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、だったら付きあうよ。荷物持ちぐらいしか出来ないけど」
lines.english: “I see. Then I'll come with you. I can't do much besides carry the bags, but...”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、いいよ。買ってるあいだ、待たせちゃうとわるいし」
lines.english: “What? No, it is fine. I would feel bad making you wait while I shop.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなの遠慮しないでいいって。僕だって小鳩ばっかりに──」
lines.english: “You don't have to hold back. I can't keep leaving everything to you—”

lines.japanese: 「いい、邪魔だし」
lines.english: “No, it’d just be a nuisance.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そう……？　待たされるのは嫌いじゃない方なんだけど、邪魔じゃ仕様がないよね、ハハ……」
lines.english: “Oh. I see...? I don't mind waiting, but if I'd be in the way, I suppose it can't be helped. Haha...”

lines.japanese: 「ああっ！　ちが、ちがう、そうじゃなくてっ！」
lines.english: “Ah! No! That isn't what I meant!”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんカップルのお邪魔になるってことでしょ」
lines.english: “She means she'd be in the way of you as a couple.”

lines.japanese: こくっ、こくっ。
lines.english: Nod, nod.

lines.japanese: 小鳩は何度も頷いた。
lines.english: Kobato nodded several times.

lines.japanese: 「たしかに言葉足らずだけど察しなよ。こばっちゃんが羽田君にそんなこと言うわけないじゃん。ねえ？」
lines.english: “She didn't use enough words, but figure it out. Kobbie would never say something like that to you, Haneda. Right?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、そんなおこまがしいこと言いません。つねに兄へのけいいを持っています」
lines.english: “Yes. I would never say anything so persumptuous. I maintain constant respect for my brother.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　ほんとかなあ」
lines.english: “Really? I wonder.”

lines.japanese: 「ほんとだよ。とくにタカシお兄ちゃんには、ずっと」
lines.english: “It is true. Especially with you, Takashi. Always.”

lines.japanese: おどけて言ってみせた僕に対し、小鳩はごく素のままで答えた。
lines.english: I had been teasing her, but Kobato answered with complete sincerity.

lines.japanese: だから僕はすべて報われる気がした。
lines.english: And I felt as though that rewarded me for everything.

lines.japanese: これまで小鳩は、ときおり妙にするどい舌鋒で僕を突きはなすことがあったけれど、それらもきっと、適切な意思を伝えきれなかった些細なミスなんだろう。
lines.english: Kobato had sometimes pushed me away with strangely sharp words, but perhaps those had all been tiny mistakes born of her inability to communicate what she truly meant.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、本当に手伝わなくていいの？」
lines.english: “Then you're sure you don't need help?”

lines.japanese: 「いいってば、お兄ちゃんはやることあるでしょ」
lines.english: “I said I am sure. You have something else to do, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 「ちゃんと渡来さんをおうちまで送ればおとこが上がるよ、やったね！」
lines.english: “If you escort Watarai all the way home, your stock as a man will go up. Lucky you!”

lines.japanese: まさか小鳩に恋愛絡みで冷やかされる日が来るとは。
lines.english: I never imagined the day would come when Kobato teased me about romance.

lines.japanese: 可愛い妹のためにも、僕は男を上げることにした。
lines.english: For the sake of my adorable sister, I decided to raise my stock as a man.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、僕らも帰ろうか」
lines.english: “Watarai, shall we go home too?”
